# It works

::: narration
Part 1. It works.
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 3.0 s (4 words).
:::

## Claim

::: key
Adopting a surgical safety checklist lowers deaths and complications.
:::

::: narration
The claim. Adopting a surgical safety checklist lowers deaths and complications.
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 6.3 s (11 words).
:::

## Grounds

- In eight hospitals in eight cities, inpatient deaths after major surgery fell from 1.5% to 0.8% after a 19-item checklist was introduced.

. . .

- Major complications fell from 11.0% to 7.0% in the same study, which followed 3,733 patients before and 3,955 after.

::: narration
Ground one. In eight hospitals in eight cities, inpatient deaths after major surgery fell from 1.5 percent to 0.8 percent after a 19-item checklist was introduced. Ground two. Major complications fell from 11.0 percent to 7.0 percent in the same study, which followed 3,733 patients before and 3,955 after.
:::

::: notes
Ground 1 source: Haynes et al., N Engl J Med 2009;360:491-9, doi:10.1056/NEJMsa0810119
Ground 2 source: Haynes et al., N Engl J Med 2009;360:491-9, doi:10.1056/NEJMsa0810119
Estimated narration: 24.3 s (49 words).
:::

## Warrant and backing

**Warrant.** If outcomes improve across varied hospitals after a single change, that change is a likely cause.

. . .

**Backing.** The hospitals were in both rich and poor countries, and the study's lead author reported a visible impact at every site, which makes a local fluke less likely (Harvard Gazette, 2009).

::: narration
The warrant. If outcomes improve across varied hospitals after a single change, that change is a likely cause. The backing. The hospitals were in both rich and poor countries, and the study's lead author reported a visible impact at every site, which makes a local fluke less likely (Harvard Gazette, 2009).
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 25.2 s (51 words).
:::

## Qualifier and rebuttals

**Qualifier.** Probably

. . .

- The study compared the same hospitals before and after, with no control group, so other changes over the same period could explain part of the improvement.

. . .

- The results describe major operations in the study's hospitals; smaller or very different settings may see smaller gains.

::: narration
The qualifier. Probably. Rebuttal one. The study compared the same hospitals before and after, with no control group, so other changes over the same period could explain part of the improvement. Rebuttal two. The results describe major operations in the study's hospitals; smaller or very different settings may see smaller gains.
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 26.1 s (51 words).
:::

# It is cheap

::: narration
Part 2. It is cheap.
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 3.5 s (5 words).

## Claim

::: key
A surgical checklist is a low-cost change compared with the harm it targets.
:::

::: narration
The claim. A surgical checklist is a low-cost change compared with the harm it targets.
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 8.1 s (15 words).
:::

## Grounds

- The checklist has 19 items and is used at three pauses: before anaesthesia, before the incision and before the patient leaves the operating room.

. . .

- The study's authors described it as neither costly nor lengthy to put into practice.

::: narration
Ground one. The checklist has 19 items and is used at three pauses: before anaesthesia, before the incision and before the patient leaves the operating room. Ground two. The study's authors described it as neither costly nor lengthy to put into practice.
:::

::: notes
Ground 1 source: Haynes et al., N Engl J Med 2009;360:491-9
Ground 2 source: Haynes et al., N Engl J Med 2009;360:491-9
Estimated narration: 21.1 s (42 words).
:::

## Warrant and backing

**Warrant.** A measure that adds little cost and little time, and prevents costly harm, is worth requiring.

. . .

**Backing.** Preventing a complication saves treatment, hospital days and suffering; a Harvard team estimated that universal use in US operating rooms could save \$15 billion to \$25 billion a year (Harvard Gazette, 2009).

::: narration
The warrant. A measure that adds little cost and little time, and prevents costly harm, is worth requiring. The backing. Preventing a complication saves treatment, hospital days and suffering; a Harvard team estimated that universal use in US operating rooms could save $15 billion to $25 billion a year (Harvard Gazette, 2009).
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 25.7 s (52 words).
:::

## Qualifier and rebuttals

**Qualifier.** In most cases

. . .

- The US savings figure is a projection from the research team, not a measured result.

::: narration
The qualifier. In most cases. The rebuttal. The US savings figure is a projection from the research team, not a measured result.
:::

## Claim

::: key
Hospitals should require the checklist rather than leave it optional.
:::

::: narration
The claim. Hospitals should require the checklist rather than leave it optional.
:::

::: notes
Estimated narration: 6.7 s (12 words).
:::

## Grounds

- In the study, teams confirmed each checklist item aloud, and adherence to six key safety measures rose by about two-thirds.

. . .

- The study's lead author said that with a checklist other team members are more likely to speak up if they see something going wrong.

::: narration
Ground one. In the study, teams confirmed each checklist item aloud, and adherence to six key safety measures rose by about two-thirds. Ground two. The study's lead author said that with a checklist other team members are more likely to speak up if they see something going wrong.
:::

::: notes
Ground 1 source: Haynes et al., N Engl J Med 2009;360:491-9
Ground 2 source: WBUR, 15 January 2009
Estimated narration: 23.9 s (48 words).
:::

## Warrant and backing

**Warrant.** A safeguard that depends on everyone using it every time loses most of its value when it is optional.

. . .

**Backing.** Checklists like this are standard practice before every flight in aviation.

::: narration
The warrant. A safeguard that depends on everyone using it every time loses most of its value when it is optional. The backing. Checklists like this are standard practice before every flight in aviation.
:::
